chunks: And Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Alī al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily Allāh offered our Wilāyah to the inhabitants of different lands, but no one accepted it except the inhabitants of Kūfah. And verily, near it is a grave; no anguished person comes to it and prays four Rak’ah at it, except that Allāh sends him back pleased with the fulfillment of his request.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the grave near Kūfah mentioned in Kamil al-Ziyarat?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) highlights the unique spiritual status of Kūfah, noting that while Allah offered the Wilayah to various cities, the people of Kūfah were the primary acceptors, establishing their enduring connection to the Imams. The hadith further emphasizes the efficacy of visiting the specific grave near Kūfah, where performing four Rak’ahs serves as a means for Allah to return the supplicant joyfully after fulfilling their needs, reflecting the Shia belief in the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt's resting places.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan Al-Saffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faďďāl, from Mufaďďal ibn Sāliḥ, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Ali Al-Ḥalabi, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

Verily Allāh offered our Wilāyah to the inhabitants of different lands but no one accepted it (immediately) except the inhabitants of Kūfah. Verily there is a grave near it to which no anguished person goes and next to which he prays four Rak’ah without Allāh sending him back pleased, with his requests fulfilled.
